# Independent original ISP lifecycle comparator captures

Unchanged `check_camerad_isp_lifecycle.py` supplies all expectations, pinned by
SHA256 and CPython version. The full ordered generator has 30 cases (18 sensor,
mode and depth combinations plus 12 retry boundaries); smoke selects exactly
case zero and case four. Forty-five independently executed original-main process
cases preserve commands, ordered environments, 45-second timeout/core hook,
receipt bytes, progress, failure stop, JSON short circuit and artifact order.

Thirty-three normalization cases capture allocation flags, native owned-FD close
counts, config unmaps, acquire/release bytes, ordering, malformed records and
assertion messages. AssertionError becomes a recorded ownership failure; other
exceptions escape before report updates. Trace JSON is parsed before run.json.
Six real CLI captures and a raw-byte qemu/output-path run pin inherited stdin
through all 60 children. Actual original current C++/Rust evidence passes all 30
cases; all three current binary hashes were revalidated before reusing that
receipt. This reuse is not a fresh execution.

The camera lifecycle checker imports normalize from this Python module. Retiring
the CLI must retain that live helper until its caller is converted. Likewise,
kernel digest/disable_core remain imports. Only the original CLI is removed; normalize remains AST-identical.

Capture drivers are under ignored
`.analysis/scratch/2026-10-18-camera-isp-lifecycle-check/`. The intended missing-module/bin RED was observed before production. The native
source now implements the dynamic generator and ownership algorithm. Five native tests, strict Clippy and the actual 30-case PATH-disabled comparison
pass; the entire report matches the retained independent original. The same
comparison also passes after Python CLI removal. No device acceptance is claimed.
